Usage: a2web web fetch_raw [OPTIONS]

  Fallback only — prefer query for ~95%% of web reads.

  Returns the page's markdown content with no server-side LLM extraction. Use
  only when:

  1. You need the full structural content (link graphs, repeated    rows for
  scraping, tables to transform). 2. A previous query call returned answer:
  null with an    llm_unavailable operator hint and you need the page text
  to answer your own question. 3. query's answer is suspect and you need to
  verify against    source.

  Do not default to this tool — query is cheaper end-to-end because the
  server-side Haiku extractor is much smaller than the model calling this
  tool. Same tier cascade, same diagnostics, just without the extraction
  phase.

Options:
  --url TEXT                      Absolute http(s) URL to fetch.
  --include-links / --no-include-links
                                  Include the extracted `links` array in the
                                  response. Default False — links are a large
                                  share of payload bytes on aggregator pages.
                                  [default: no-include-links]
  --link-roles TEXT               JSON value.
  --debug / --no-debug            Return the full `diagnostics` trace. Default
                                  False.  [default: no-debug]
  --wrap-content / --no-wrap-content
                                  Wrap content_md with HTML-comment markers
                                  carrying source URL + 'untrusted content'
                                  warning. Default True.  [default: wrap-
                                  content]
  --next-links / --no-next-links  Return up to 10 curated 'what to fetch next'
                                  links in `next_links` (drilldown / related /
                                  source / discussion). Tier-1 site handler
                                  candidates work without ask=; default True.
                                  [default: next-links]
  --format [auto|json|tsv|page-tsv]
                                  Output format. 'auto' uses type-driven
                                  routing.  [default: auto]
  --json                          End-to-end JSON: success+error on stdout.
                                  Mutually exclusive with --format.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.
